transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Janelle (Redwood Solutions), Ellen (VantageCommerce CTO), Ravi (Vantage ML Eng), Sofia (Vantage Infra)

Summary:
- VantageCommerce is evaluating an exit from their current OpenAI/Azure stack into a more cost-predictable serving layer; they want parity on responses and confidence on latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Primary concerns: eval parity (quality), KV cache compatibility (vLLM behavior), private VPC/networking, KMS + data residency, and pilot timeline.

Topics covered:
- Current infra and why they want to exit (cost spikes, rate limits)
- Model portability: TGI/vLLM differences, tokenization quirks, LoRA/ft artifacts
- Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private tradeoffs and pricing
- Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs, retention policies
- Benchmark plan: perf, latency P95, throughput, sample prompt sets

Action items (high level in call):
- Redwood to share security pack and parity benchmark plan
- Vantage to provide sample prompt set and a token distribution histogram
- Schedule follow-up deep dive on VPC peering and dedicated capacity options

Transcript body:
[00:00:05] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros? we got about 50 minutes.
[00:00:20] Ellen: hi i'm ellen, cto at vantagecommerce, we run product search and personalization mostly real-time, i'm leading the eval.
[00:00:28] Ravi: ravi, ml eng, i own inference stack and the current pipeline, mostly on azure openai plus some vllm on prem for caching.
[00:00:38] Liam: liam from redwood, se, i'll drive the technical bits and benchmarks.
[00:00:44] Janelle: janelle here, solutions, i'll follow up on onboarding and pricing.
[00:00:50] Sofia: sophia, infra, i'll be the networking and security contact.

[00:01:22] Maya: great. can you give a little context on why you're exploring an exit or a different serving layer?
[00:01:36] Ellen: yeah so we've seen costs spike, especially with bursty search traffic. also rate limits during peak sales windows have bitten us twice. we want more predictability and the ability to tune quantization and batching.
[00:01:50] Ravi: to add, we tinkered with vllm in house but it's brittle at scale, kv cache handling differs and we get tokenization drift when switching back and forth to openai models.

[00:02:30] Liam: when you say tokenization drift, do you mean output style changes or actually token-level differences causing prompt truncation?
[00:02:40] Ravi: both, sometimes the model picks a different subtoken boundary and that shifts completions. also some of our ft artifacts rely on exact tokenization.

[00:03:10] Maya: got it, so parity isn't just semantic output, it's also deterministic behavior for prompts used in ft and reranking. that's useful.

[00:03:48] Ellen: yeah, the two success criteria for us are: (1) parity on our test evals — syntactic and business metric parity — and (2) predictable unit cost under load.

[00:04:10] Maya: good. can you share the current stack? ravi?
[00:04:16] Ravi: sure, we mainly call OpenAI via azure openai gateway for chat/gen, embeddings with a mix of open-source models via vLLM on k8s for on-prem cases, and TGI experiments for some smaller seq2seq jobs. we also have a small dedicated g4 pool for fast inference.

[00:04:50] Liam: ok that's a familiar mix. couple questions: are you using any special tokenizer or byte-pair changes for finetunes? and are you using LoRA or full-ft?
[00:05:00] Ravi: LoRA for most recent experiments, some full-ft older runs. tokenizer is standard bpe but we applied a small vocab patch for product codes.

[00:05:30] Janelle: from a Redwood perspective we usually recommend pinning a model variant and running a canary then a canary rollback plan. for LoRA/ft artifacts we have migration hooks but they'll need a parity check.

[00:06:12] Ellen: how do you handle kv cache differences? that's been our largest headache — latency got worse when we tried to move vllm to a multi-node config.

[00:06:24] Liam: great question — Redwood's runtime keeps a per-request kv cache abstraction and we support prefix caching; when we route requests we try to colocate KV for hot sessions, that reduces cache misses. but we'll replicate your vllm trace and check for mismatch.

[00:06:55] Ravi: replication of trace is key. can you emulate our sequence length distribution? we have heavy tails with some long product descriptions.

[00:07:10] Maya: yes the benchmark plan will ask for actual seq length histogram and token distribution. we'll run custom runs to match that and report p50/p95/p99.

[00:07:40] Ellen: can you also speak to private deployment? we have compliance needs for european data residency and want a VPC option.

[00:07:53] Liam: Redwood Private supports VPC peering and on-prem packages; for EU residency we can provision dedicated capacity in our eu-west region or do an on-prem runtime. what sort of SLA or logs do you need?

[00:08:10] Sofia: we need audit logs for every token request, retention for 7 years is preferred, and KMS integration for key rotation. also SSO via SAML, enterprise RBAC.

[00:08:28] Maya: we can share our security pack — SOC 2 type II, ISO artifacts, how audit logs can be forwarded; KMS is supported via customer-managed keys (we'll include a quick note).

[00:08:50] Ellen: any gotchas with SSO and service accounts? we've had trouble mapping granular usage to teams.

[00:09:00] Janelle: we support token-level attribution and per-route dashboards. service accounts map to project-scoped roles and you can export cost breakouts per token.

[00:09:28] Ravi: on performance, what's realistic p95 latency for our 1k token median with heavy concurrency?

[00:09:38] Liam: depends on model variant and quantization. for a 1k token median on A100-class with int8 quant we typically see p95 in the 400-700ms range for optimized models; with aggressive batching latency raises but cost drops. we'll put numbers in the benchmark report against your workload.

[00:10:10] Ellen: and cost comparison vs OpenAI? we need order-of-magnitude to justify a migration.

[00:10:18] Maya: initial numbers show dedicated capacity is often 30-60% cheaper at scale vs public API for heavy workloads, but it depends on utilization and batching. we'll run the math in the SOW.

[00:10:45] Ravi: curious about fallback policies — if a heavy event overwhelms dedicated nodes, can requests gracefully fallback to hosted or a lower-cost variant?

[00:10:55] Liam: yes, smart routing can fall back to a compatible model variant or route to hosted capacity. we can set latency/cost thresholds for automatic fallback.

[00:11:30] Ellen: what's required for a pilot?

[00:11:35] Janelle: typically we ask for a 2-week pilot: share prompts, a small dataset for evals, and a short window of traffic replay. we provision a small dedicated pool or hosted endpoints depending on desired isolation.

[00:11:50] Sofia: for VPC we might need a maintenance window to test peering and routing rules.

[00:12:05] Maya: noted. we'll include a pilot plan in the benchmark doc.

[00:12:35] Ravi: question — any incompatibilities with TGI endpoints? we ran some TGI experiments and saw different sampling behaviors.

[00:12:46] Liam: TGI has some defaults that differ, sampling temp and topk/top-p defaults. Redwood runtime normalizes sampling behavior and you can pin decoding params; however subtle differences remain and that's why we do eval parity.

[00:13:12] Ellen: okay. one operational question: how do you monitor model regressions? we need alerts if quality drops post-rollout.

[00:13:22] Maya: Redwood Optimize has eval monitoring tied to prompt sets, we can run daily evals and trigger regression alerts based on business metrics you define (ctr, accuracy, rerank precision).

[00:13:40] Ravi: cool. about tokenizer patching — will that break upgrade paths?

[00:13:48] Liam: it can. best path is to keep a stable tokenizer in production and include conversion scripts; we'll help with a compatibility shim if needed.

[00:14:15] Ellen: any legal or procurement blockers you've seen with other retailers?

[00:14:24] Maya: common asks are long retention windows, data residency, and indemnity language. we have enterprise add-ons for custom retention and can work with legal on contract terms.

[00:15:05] Ravi: are there customers who've migrated from OpenAI to Redwood who kept parity? any case study?

[00:15:12] Janelle: we've got a few anonymized case studies; i'll share a short deck showing perf and cost delta.

[00:15:35] Ellen: great — also can you log token-level cost per route? finance will require that.

[00:15:42] Maya: yes, we have token-level cost breakdowns per model and per route.

[00:16:10] (small cross talk)
[00:16:40] Sofia: networking detail: we use strict egress rules, can we run peering without opening wide breaks?

[00:16:54] Liam: yes, peering and private endpoints supported, we can give exact IP ranges and allow-listing for the test window.

[00:17:30] Ravi: for the benchmark, do you need us to share live traffic or synthetic replay?

[00:17:40] Maya: either works; replay is easiest for comparability. if you can't share live data we can use a synthetic workload that mirrors distribution.

[00:18:08] Ellen: timeline — we want to decide on a vendor within 4 weeks to hit holiday season improvements. is that reasonable?

[00:18:18] Janelle: yes we can do a 2-week pilot immediately and have results in 3 weeks.

[00:18:40] Ravi: last question: do you support on-prem GPUs behind a firewall?

[00:18:48] Liam: yes, Redwood Private can be deployed on-prem or in your VPC with customer-managed control plane for air-gapped needs. there are additional support and infra fees.

[00:19:15] Ellen: awesome.
[00:19:22] Maya: wrap up — we'll send the security pack, benchmark plan, and proposed pilot SOW. liam will draft the eval prompt set. janelle to send pricing options. can we meet next thursday for a deep dive at 16:00 UTC?
[00:19:40] Sofia: works for us.
[00:19:44] Ravi: yeah that time's fine.
[00:20:05] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and timelines.
[00:20:15] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: some speaker labels were auto-attributed; there are a few misheard words (e.g., vllm as 'v-l-m', TGI as 'tee-gee-eye' in one interval).
